page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores running on the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 platform at a nominal clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The architecture uses a one-to-one thread-to-core mapping with simultaneous multithreading disabled. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 300 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and does not include hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional performance in multi-core compute and high-capacity memory operations. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing at 163,416.3 and Geekbench multi-core at 26,210.0, alongside strong ratings in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Clang code compilation. Memory subsystem throughput is equally prominent, recording 481.31 GB/sec in large uncached reads and sustaining over 198 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-threaded metrics remain within the average category, with Geekbench single-core at 1,890.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 30.4 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is driven by the resource density of the ARMv9 architecture, which provides dedicated non-hyperthreaded performance across all 96 cores for consistent multi-tenant or concurrent operations. Tradeoffs include the complete reliance on network-attached storage for persistence and baseline single-core performance that does not benefit serial-bound applications. The r8gn.24xlarge is structurally suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, distributed in-memory data grids such as Redis, large-scale database deployments, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz and 768.0 GB of RAM, backed by the AWS Nitro System. Designed with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, it delivers 300 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark testing shows top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust memory bandwidth reaching 481.31 GB/sec on large reads, and high in-memory database throughput with over 198 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core performance remains average, the non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture offers consistent throughput across highly parallelized workloads. The instance is suited for large in-memory caches, distributed databases, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise applications running on ARM64.
